alalal-c47141-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 15: whether infants belong to the temple of God.

alalal-c47141-d1e113.summary: Introduces the question on Lombard's statement that infants belong to the temple of God.

alalal-c47141-d1e122.summary: Objection: infants do not seem to belong to God's temple, since they do not know him.

alalal-c47141-d1e132.summary: Reply: infants belong to the temple through the sacrament, not by the use of grace but by its habit; Lombard calls this the gift of the Holy Spirit rather than its use, since use requires the exercise of free choice.
claims: Baptised infants are God's temple by the habit of grace received through the sacrament, though they cannot yet use it.

alalal-c47141.summary: Article 15 asks whether infants, who do not know God, belong to his temple, as Lombard says. Albert answers that they do through the sacrament: they have the habit of grace, the gift of the Holy Spirit, though not its use, which requires the exercise of free choice.
claims: Baptised infants are God's temple through the habit of grace, though they lack its use.
